title: Check yourself: Failure types, origins and recoveries

questions.stem: A service starts Claude's reply with prefilled text on a newly adopted Claude 4.6 model, and every call returns a 400. What is the right recovery?

options.text: Retry each call with exponential back-off and jitter
options.says: Ruled out because "A request that fails the same way every time it is sent is an integration failure until proved otherwise, and retrying it only repeats the failure".

options.text: Extend the timeout so that each call has longer to finish
options.says: Ruled out because a timeout is the 504 recovery, where the table says "Change the call: stream, or use a batch", while every migration row has the same recovery: "change the request".

options.text: Reword the system prompt so that Claude continues the text
options.says: Ruled out because "None is cured by a retry, a longer timeout or a different prompt", and a reworded system prompt is a different prompt.

options.text: Rebuild the request so that the user speaks last
options.says: The errors page lists the rejected prefill under "Common validation errors": "This model does not support assistant message prefill. The conversation must end with a user message." The module adds that a migration error has the recovery "change the request".

origin.section: Migration errors: your request, after a model change

questions.stem: A reply to a long-document summary ends mid-sentence, with status 200 and a stop reason of `max_tokens`. What is the origin and the right fix?

options.text: The integration's limit, so raise it or continue the turn
options.says: The table reads `max_tokens` as "Integration: the limit is yours" with the recovery "Raise `max_tokens` or continue the response".

options.text: The model, so reword the prompt to ask for shorter output
options.says: Ruled out because the trap says "A reply cut by `max_tokens` needs a larger limit or a continuation, and no wording will change it".

options.text: The service, so retry the same call after a short pause
options.says: Ruled out because a retry repeats the same limit, and the page says "A cut-off reply is usually your setting".

options.text: The account, so ask for a higher quota on the organisation
options.says: Ruled out because the status is 200 and no quota was exceeded: stop reasons are "part of the response body" and not account errors.

origin.section: Failures that carry a status of 200

questions.stem: An assistant's reply arrives with status 200 and a stop reason of `refusal`. The team's dashboard shows nothing wrong. What does the documentation imply?

options.text: Nothing failed, so the dashboard is right to show no alert
options.says: Ruled out because the refusal is a real failure of the request, and the course's advice is to "track refusals as their own signal".

options.text: A resend will usually work, so the team should retry as is
options.says: Ruled out because "Re-sending a refused request to the same model usually results in another refusal".

options.text: Error-rate alerts miss it, so a separate signal is needed
options.says: The page says "Refusals are responses, not errors", so "monitoring built only on error rates won't surface it".

options.text: The service is overloaded, so the call should wait for a header
options.says: Ruled out because waiting for a retry header is the recovery for capacity failures: "Wait for the header, or back off with jitter, then retry", while this reply has status 200.

origin.section: Failures that carry a status of 200
